questions.prompt: A two-week project plan lists fourteen features. What is the most useful next step?
choices: Start coding the first feature on the list
Split the list into core features and nice-to-haves, and build only the core first
Drop the idea and pick something smaller
Add the features you have not thought of yet
questions.explain: The list is not too long, it is unsorted. Splitting it gives you a version that works early, and the rest is still written down if there is time.

questions.prompt: Which of these belong in the out-of-scope section of a task manager's plan?
choices: Saving tasks to a file, without which nothing survives closing the program
Several people using the same list at once
questions.explain: Out of scope records what you have decided not to build. Saving to a file is what makes the project useful at all, so it is core.

questions.prompt: Which of these goals tells you when you are finished?
choices: Build a really good task manager
Build a task manager over the next two weeks
Build a command-line task manager that can add, complete and list tasks and save them to a file, in two weeks
Learn more Python by building something
questions.explain: Only one of these can be checked off. A goal with no finish line is a project you can keep working on forever.

questions.prompt: Why write down the features you are not going to build?
choices: It makes the plan look more thorough
It records the decision, so you stop re-arguing it with yourself mid-project
Python needs to know what is excluded
It stops anyone else building the same thing
questions.explain: Scope creep is usually you, three days in, deciding this one extra feature would be quick. A written decision is what you argue with instead of the whole question again.

questions.prompt: Put the planning steps in the order that keeps the work pointed at something.
items: Pick a problem you actually have
Write down the core features that solve it
Move everything else to nice-to-have or out of scope
Start coding the first core feature
questions.explain: Scope comes out of the problem and code comes out of scope. Coding first means finding out what the project was for after building the wrong half of it.
